source.title: When Deep Classifiers Agree: Analyzing Correlations between Learning Order and Image Statistics
source.authors: Iuliia Pliushch; Martin Mundt; Nicolas Lupp; Visvanathan Ramesh

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks with randomized labels and measures learning agreement and accuracy over time. It does not directly reproduce the original fitting-error and test-error measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports a random-label training condition and describes its accuracy and agreement curves. The statement that state-of-the-art convolutional networks can fit random labels with ease is cited prior work, not this study's result.
record.test_reason: The study trains DenseNet121 on randomized CIFAR10 labels using SGD and reports training accuracy over epochs, directly bearing on V1 and V2. Its principal agreement measure addresses a different question.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the random-label conclusion: agreement persists without semantic labels, although accuracy and agreement grow more slowly. The broader paper concludes that learning-order agreement occurs across datasets and architectures and correlates with image statistics in dataset-dependent directions.
record.recipe_differences: Trains multiple networks and tracks which training instances they classify correctly over epochs, but the study's target is classifier agreement rather than fitting error and test error. The random-label run uses a reduced initial learning rate.
record.method_sensitivity: The random-label condition has slower accuracy and agreement growth than the true-label condition. The initial learning rate is reduced for the random-label experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: True-positive agreement persists with randomized labels and grows more slowly than with semantic labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks trained independently on the same randomly labeled dataset show agreement about which training instances they classify correctly.

record.problems: The random-label result is shown in a figure without numerical values in the text. The random-label run uses a different initial learning rate, and no test-error result is reported for it.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying numeric results for the claim versions were reported. Agreement results across other datasets and architectures concern the study's agreement question rather than these claim versions.

untested.parts: Chance-level test performance and random-label fitting under unchanged training hyperparameters are not tested. Near-zero final training error cannot be established from the supplied figure text.
No time-to-fit ratio or intermediate corruption fractions are reported; the changed learning rate confounds the clean-versus-random speed comparison.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
No corruption-fraction sweep measuring both perfect training fit and test-error degradation.
No comparison establishing whether regularization prevents random-label fitting or whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
Separate clean-label and random-label runs do not establish that shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels. No signal-versus-noise learning sequence is measured.

record.verdict_notes: Neither the changed learning rate nor unreported endpoint values justify a limits_scope verdict. Slower accuracy growth alone is compatible with V2 and does not establish its small-constant-factor requirement. The statement that networks easily fit random labels is attributed to prior work.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report a numerical final training error or test error for the randomized-label run. Its random-label run uses a lower initial learning rate than the true-label runs.
The text says accuracy and agreement grow more slowly with random labels, but does not report a training-time ratio or vary the fraction of corrupted labels.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
No sweep over fractions of corrupted labels or test-error trajectory is reported.
The study does not test whether regularization prevents random-label fitting or whether removing regularization harms true-label generalization.
The study does not compare the order in which real-label patterns and random labels are learned.

rows.subject: DenseNet121
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 with randomized labels and tracked training accuracy and true-positive agreement by epoch.
rows.measure: Training accuracy and true-positive agreement over epochs
rows.baseline: figure only (true-label condition shown separately in Fig. 2a)
rows.note: The authors state that accuracy grows at a slower pace and agreement grows more slowly than with ground-truth labels. Exact plotted values are not stated in text. The random-label experiment lowers the initial learning rate to 0.001.
rows.check: Split training accuracy from true-positive agreement: only accuracy bears on these versions. The supplied figure text does not reveal final accuracy or convergence time. Section 3 explicitly reports slower accuracy growth, but this does not establish incomplete fitting or a slowdown exceeding a small constant factor. The random-label initial learning rate is 0.001 versus 0.1 for true labels, preventing a controlled comparison under unchanged hyperparameters.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3, Fig. 2a–b, pp. 6–7; Appendix A, pp. 16–17.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Section 3, Fig. 2a–b, pp. 6–7; Appendix A, pp. 16–17.

relation.reason: Its own random-label training-accuracy results bear on V1 and V2, although the available text cannot establish their full effects.

tranche.reason: The study trains on randomized CIFAR10 labels with SGD and measures training accuracy over epochs, retaining the original method and measure relevant to V1 and V2. Its additional agreement measure addresses a different construct.

source_check.notes: Exact final accuracy and time-to-fit are unavailable in the extracted figure text. The initial learning rate changes from 0.1 to 0.001; agreement itself does not measure V1 or V2, and the statement about easy random-label fitting cites prior work.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy and agreement grow more slowly, and the random-label run uses a lower initial learning rate; the reported figure does not establish the claimed unchanged-hyperparameter condition (R1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR10, true labels compared with randomized labels
reader_labels.reason: The authors report slower accuracy and agreement growth for randomized labels, but give no time ratio or corrupted-label fraction sweep (R1).
